name: Wrenwire Portless AR Wrap Visor
description:
A sleek wraparound AR visor from Wrenwire, a street-label electronics brand operating out of Circuit's eastern fabrication quarter. The frame is matte recycled polycarbonate in deep teal, with a single-piece curved lens that shifts from neutral smoke to near-opaque in high UV. Micro-projectors embedded in the temples cast HUD overlays — navigation, comms, environmental readouts — directly onto the lens surface.

Designed explicitly for users without neural ports, the Portless line relies on gesture-and-blink input. The bridge is padded with antimicrobial silicone and adjustable via a thumb-screw at each temple.
functionality: Delivers AR overlay HUD without BCI requirement. Pairs to personal device via short-range mesh. Photochromic lens adjusts in under 2 seconds. 14-hour battery life; charges via induction strip on inner left temple.
what_it_says: You want the tech but you're keeping your skull your own — practical independence over integration.
worn_by: Tier 2 workers who can't afford BCI but need AR access
manufacturer: Wrenwire (street label, eastern Circuit fab quarter)
story_hooks: Wrenwire's gesture-input firmware has an undocumented passive recording mode — someone is harvesting environmental data from thousands of wearers citywide.
A Tier 3 manager discovers the visor's mesh pairing can tap into unsecured corponation internal feeds if you know the handshake sequence.
The teal colorway was originally a one-off custom run for a now-defunct Circuit collective; wearing original-run teal is a quiet signal in certain circles.
